requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.toml.fingerprints`. I took four obligations from its text and from the cited `requirements.references.structural_hash` and `requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

**1. Comments are excluded from TOML structural hashes.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs#fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` has a TOML case: selector `table[t]`, source `[t]\n# note\na = 1 # trailing\n`.
  - Editing both a leading comment and a trailing comment leaves the hash unchanged.
  - Removing both comments leaves the hash unchanged.
  - Changing the non-comment value (`a = 2`) changes the hash. This shows comment exclusion is not simply "nothing is hashed".
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` has a second TOML case where a comment is edited and the hash must stay equal.

**2. Whitespace-separated words, with each word encoded separately.**
- The same test uses `a = "two words"` as the original.
  - `"two   words"` (different whitespace) must give an equal fingerprint.
  - `"twowords"` must give a different fingerprint. This is the `ab cd` versus `abcd` distinction the cited requirement names.

**3. SHA-256 over an unambiguous encoding.**
- The TOML test asserts the fingerprint value is 64 hexadecimal characters.
- The shared encoder, `src/outline/hash.rs#struct[Encoder]`, is language-independent. It is checked against known SHA-256 vectors in `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]`.
  - That test uses the empty-input digest and a tagged, length-prefixed `hello` digest.
  - It also checks that nesting and sibling structure are distinguished, and that different grammar kinds hash differently.
- That test is marked for `structural_hash` and plain-text, not TOML. Because the encoder is shared across languages, I treat the TOML length and format check plus this test as sufficient. I don't count the missing TOML marker as an adequacy gap.

**4. The fingerprint scheme identifies the rules and their version.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` checks that `languages::Toml` and its `Default` report scheme `toml-structural-v1`.
- It also checks that loaded `OutlineContent` retains the same scheme through `fingerprint_scheme()`.

The cited requirements are context only. I checked that the TOML case applies them and did not reassess their implementation or tests. I found no unacknowledged gap, and no {fixme} acknowledgments were supplied or needed.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
